rationale: ROUND 2, revising on the same correlation after REVISE. Four objections landed and all four were acted on rather than argued with; the migration was already APPLIED when they arrived (config is live on apply), so this round records what changed in the world, not just in the plan. (1) reuse_agent, medium — 'no evidence the author searched check_image_url_404.go or check_placeholder_image_in_use.go for overlap before arming a third detection path'. Correct, I had not, and it was the most substantive objection. Measured since: check_image_url_404.go contains ZERO references to href or -only, so the vanished-ANCHOR class (238 lost five card links and a section CTA that rendered as nothing at all) has NO other detector on this estate; that is the non-overlapping half and it is the larger one. On the symptom they DO overlap, and the overlap is worse than the seat could have known: ai-agent-orchestration.com already holds image_url_404:empty-src at status 'detected' for the very page that serves five empty src today, so the existing detector saw it and the item has sat unworked. The keys differ deliberately (site-wide vs page+slot) because a site-wide key jams — 3 sites hold an open empty-src item, and a site holding one cannot mint another for a different page. The timing differs too: image_url_404 is an async discovery check and the rotations are PAUSED on the owner's cost instruction (bugs_open/230; 41 open items, all last touched 2026-08-17), so the record-only emit is currently the only LIVE detector for this class. (2) tooling_provenance, medium — no doc_notes trail for a multi-part sequencing decision. Written: subject_type 'decision', subject_key 'bugs_open/238:dead_url_control_arming_sequence', carrying the two-step arming, the NEW ground the refusal is held on, the four measurable drain conditions, the overlap analysis above, and the partial-coverage statement. (3) bug_historian, medium — partial coverage of a shared mechanism (1 of 11 RenderTemplate call sites) should be named explicitly, not filed as a clean future RFC. Named, in the doc_notes row and in the register, with the eight unguarded sites listed and 016b §9's shape cited by name. (4) editquality, missing — the stale register status line that the rationale itself blamed had no covering edit. Fixed in commit d5f716fba, before the verdict arrived: PBP-040's status corrected visibly (strike-through, date, cost) in both the entry and the index row, recording that the line was false in BOTH clauses for nine days and that the config half stayed unarmed BECAUSE arming it looked premature. (5) editquality, medium — the live path assumption 'needs DB confirmation, not just the author's stated read'. It now has the strongest possible confirmation: the migration APPLIED, its pre-flight assertion (which aborts if {workflow,steps,rerender_sections,action} is not 'rerender_page_sections') passed, its verify block reported 1 of 1 steps armed fleet-wide, and an independent re-query after COMMIT confirms it. (6) editquality, low — 497's two 'edits' on one file were one edit split for narrative; merged here. ONE THING THE COUNCIL COULD NOT SEE, added because it changes what happens next: the file is now numbered 504, not 497. Two other lanes took 497 AND 498 while this was being written. Same content, renumbered before any apply; recorded in the file header and in WRONG_CALLS.

plan.risks: Volume: one item per (page, slot, dead-field-set) on any re-render of a section rendering an empty src=/href=. Bounded by insertWorkItem's idx_swi_dedup-matched ON CONFLICT and its two-strike anti-churn label. ONE churn edge is stated rather than discovered: the item key embeds the SORTED dead-field list, so a PARTIAL repair changes the key and can mint a second item alongside a parked first one. Bounded, not zero; the close-out has to look for both. Between arming and the next chassis roll, the config report names record_dead_url_controls as unrecognised, because the declaration is Go. Cosmetic, warn-only (CheckConfig, not StrictConfig — verified at the deciding arm), and it is the stated cost of arming detection today rather than after a roll. Gated fields are NOT covered by this and cannot be: missingBareFields walks root-scope actions only, so a {{if .cardN_link_url}} guard keeps its field out of the report. For the gated class the only signal remains the 28 STRUCTURAL_KEY_CARRY_MISS findings, whose consumer is the NEXT submission (498/499). A gated field fails MORE quietly than an ungated one, which is the opposite of the intuition that gating is the safe pattern. A sustained zero after arming has TWO readings and the file says so: nothing is re-rendering a damaged section (plausible — the improvement loop and the discovery rotations are both paused on cost grounds, bugs_open/230), or the flag did not take. The verify block settles the second; the demand control settles the first (one 379-shape page_rerender at aao /index.html, whose five bare card*_image_url fields force missingBareFields non-empty). A traffic-free control cannot tell 'armed and quiet' from 'armed and blind'.

No on_missing-driven render gate (RFC_009 option A, owner-DEAD 2026-08-03: ~90% of fields declare no on_missing). The 8 unguarded RenderTemplate call sites named in dead_url_guard.go's own header stay unguarded — the council already ruled making RenderTemplate the reporting form is RFC-shaped, and it is reserved as candidate RFC_042. Disjoint from bugs_open/312 and its held 477: 477 edits page-content-writer's select_sections field paths, this edits page-rerender's rerender_sections step config. Different agent, different step, different key. Nothing here requires 477, and applying 477 later neither needs nor undoes it.
